nodes.label: insta-web-analytics (web tool)
nodes.rationale: Uses the official Instagram data export (ZIP), needs no credentials and carries no ToS/ban risk, and runs fully offline. Because Meta's export omits like/view counts and story viewers, the tool derives growth from follower join dates instead, and can additionally surface follower join dates, growth attribution, cohorts, ad exposure, off-platform tracking, DM stats, and a privacy audit — none of which the desktop tool can do.

nodes.label: insta-desktop-analytics (desktop tool)
nodes.rationale: Uses Instagram's private API via instagrapi with username+password credentials, which violates Instagram's ToS and risks account bans. In exchange it gets live engagement data unavailable in exports (likes/views, story viewers, giveaways) that the web tool cannot provide.

nodes.label: instagrapi library
nodes.rationale: Unofficial third-party library used to access Instagram's private API; using it violates Instagram's ToS and may cause account restrictions or bans, so the app is offered for educational/personal use only, at the user's own risk.

nodes.label: Giveaway Winner Picker
nodes.rationale: Fetches likers, commenters, and the author's followers for a given post URL, supports intersection filtering, and uses an optional seed so a pick is reproducible.

nodes.label: Anti-Detection & Session Management
nodes.rationale: Session reuse, background keep-alive pings, randomized human-like delays between API calls, and a 24-hour engagement-frequency warning exist to minimize Instagram's detection and rate-limiting of the unofficial instagrapi client.

nodes.label: Privacy & Security (credential storage)
nodes.rationale: Credentials are stored locally only, base64-encoded in UserData/saved_accounts.json, and are never uploaded or shared with any server other than Instagram's own API during login; leaving the Save checkbox unchecked avoids local storage entirely. This is the mechanism that backs the 'credentials never leave your machine' claim for the desktop tool.

nodes.label: Content-Security-Policy (connect-src 'none')
nodes.rationale: connect-src 'none' in the page's CSP is called out in an inline comment as 'the guarantee worth reading twice': the browser itself blocks any network request the page might attempt, so the claim that data never leaves the machine is enforced by the browser rather than merely promised, verifiable via DevTools -> Network showing no entries while processing an export.

nodes.label: Your media stays shut (feature tile)
nodes.rationale: Only the data manifests inside the export are read; about 90% of the archive (photos/videos) is skipped and never opened.
